sections.h2: How does the Westmoreland County recorder process a deed?
sections.html:
A cashier checks it, a barcode goes on every page, it is scanned, and the details are keyed into the index. The Recorder of Deeds in Greensburg describes those four steps on its own pages, and the whole routine is built for speed.

At the first step the cashier confirms that the paper is an original, properly signed, dated and acknowledged before a notary whose seal, signature and commission expiration date appear. Fees and transfer taxes are collected at that moment. Then a 15-digit number is assigned, and a sticker on each page shows the page count, the amount paid and the date and time of recording. After scanning, the document goes back to the person who filed it, in person or by mail. Data entry staff finish the index from the legal description, and a second team double-checks it.

The county says Westmoreland is one of only two counties in Pennsylvania where deeds are recorded and returned right away, with no wait of a day or two. That is useful to a seller, because the new owner's name reaches the public record on closing day. County offices keep normal hours of 8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. on weekdays, and they close on the county holiday calendar.

The same office also runs a Veterans' Identification Discount Card program for veterans living in the county, announced on its main page, and it publishes a free guide to searching records by name, instrument number, document category, municipality, subdivision or lot. Searches by tax map number or UPI also work, though only where the original document listed one.

sections.h2: What does the Westmoreland County recorder charge?
sections.html:
A deed or a mortgage costs $110.25 to record. Every listed document includes four names, four pages, one tax map number and one UPI, and the office asks for exact payment with anything sent in.

Westmoreland County recording fees, from the county fee schedule
Document or itemFee
Deed$110.25
Mortgage$110.25
Re-recorded deed or mortgage$112.25
Mortgage satisfaction or release$84.25
Easement or right of way$82.25
Power of attorney$41.00
Extra name$0.50
Extra page$2.00
Extra UPI$20.00

Questions about any charge go to 724-830-3518 or ROD@westmorelandcountypa.gov. Payment can be cash, money order, cashier's or certified check, or a personal check with ID. Debit and credit cards are not accepted. When you send several documents, the office will not take one check for more than five, so each document after the fifth needs its own.

sections.h2: What is the 10-digit PIN and why do Westmoreland deeds need one?
sections.html:
It is the parcel identifier number, and Westmoreland County requires it on every document it records. The county describes it as a 10-digit number, and the first digits point to the district, the map page and the lot, which the Tax Claim Bureau explains in its tax sale notes.

Getting the PIN right matters more than most sellers expect. A deed with a missing or wrong number is one of the quickest ways to have a closing package returned. If you cannot find the number on a tax bill, ask the Tax Assessment Office at 40 North Pennsylvania Avenue, Suite 440, Greensburg, or search the county's online record index. The index lets you search by name, by instrument number, or, for older records, by book and page for anything recorded before November 13, 2000.

Tax map numbers were not required until 2009, so documents from before then may not appear in a search by map number.

sections.h2: How do you e-record a deed in Westmoreland County?
sections.html:
Open an account with SimpliFile or CSC and upload the scanned original. Each vendor sets its own sign-up steps, and the county recommends reading them first.

Documents sent that way are first routed to the county's UPI and GIS Tax Mapping department for review, then forwarded to the recorder once certified. Nearly every document type can go this way, with one exception: anything that includes an attachment to the Statement of Value must come by mail or in person. The county explains the reason. An e-recorded attachment would add to the page count, and the office cannot alter the page count, so you would pay for pages that cost nothing when handed over the counter.

  • Stamped, self-addressed envelopes are required for mailed recordings and requests.
  • Include a phone number with your paperwork.
  • Plans must have original signatures, and the 18 by 24 inch plan fee is $49.00 for the first page and $20.00 for each page after that.

sections.h2: What transfer tax paperwork goes with a Westmoreland County deed?
sections.html:
Either the tax itself or a Statement of Value. Pennsylvania imposes a 1 percent state realty transfer tax, and the Department of Revenue says both buyer and seller are jointly liable. The county's recorder collects it, often alongside a local share.

The county's fee schedule says every deed has to state the true consideration or come with two copies of an Affidavit of Value. Any claimed exemption, whether full or partial, must be backed by that affidavit filed in duplicate, with street addresses, consideration, assessed value, fair market value, mortgages recorded and an explanation of why the transaction is or is not taxable. The affidavit must cite the regulation that supports the exemption.

  • Family transfers are the usual exemption, and the recording rules say the exemption must be clearly stated in the deed.
  • A deed with taxes in more than one municipality must say how the transfer taxes are divided.
  • The county publishes a Realty Transfer Tax Rates sheet; ask the office for it, since the rates differ by municipality.

sections.h2: What is Westmoreland County like for a house sale?
sections.html:
It is a Pittsburgh-area county of 1,036 square miles with 349,324 residents in the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate. QuickFacts reports 169,961 housing units, 154,979 households and a 78.4 percent owner-occupancy rate for 2020 to 2024.

The median value of an owner-occupied home is $203,500, median gross rent is $879, and median household income is $74,109. Owners with a mortgage have median monthly costs of $1,452. Population has slipped 1.5 percent since the 2020 census, from 354,663.

Greensburg is the county seat, and the county's other cities are Arnold, Jeannette, Latrobe, Lower Burrell, Monessen and New Kensington. Coal, coke, steel and glass built the county after the Civil War, and Volkswagen ran a plant near New Stanton from 1978 to 1988. The county's Land Bank and Development Authority work on vacant, abandoned and tax-delinquent properties, a reminder that older neighborhoods vary a great deal. Nineteen school districts serve the county, among them Greensburg-Salem, Hempfield Area, Norwin, Franklin Regional, Greater Latrobe and Penn-Trafford. Greensburg's January average is 28.7 degrees and its July average 71.8, so a house sees real winters.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Westmoreland County?
faqs.a: A deed costs $110.25, which includes four names, four pages, one tax map number and one UPI. Extra names cost $0.50, extra pages $2.00 and extra UPIs $20.00. Realty transfer tax is collected separately.

faqs.q: Does the Westmoreland County recorder take credit cards?
faqs.a: No. The payment policy lists cash, money orders, cashier's or certified checks and personal checks, and it states that debit and credit cards are not accepted. In person, a personal check needs a valid photo ID and the signer must be present.

faqs.q: Can I e-record every document in Westmoreland County?
faqs.a: Almost all of them. The one exception is a document with an attachment to the Statement of Value, which must be mailed or brought in. Use SimpliFile or CSC for everything else.

faqs.q: What happens if I send several documents in one envelope?
faqs.a: The office accepts one check for no more than five documents. Enclose a separate check for each document beyond the first five, plus a stamped, self-addressed return envelope.

faqs.q: Is a PIN required on a Westmoreland County deed?
faqs.a: Yes. Westmoreland County requires a 10-digit parcel identifier number on all documents, in addition to the usual acknowledgment and notary details. Ask the Tax Assessment Office if you cannot find it.
